title: Active catalog
prompt: Return sku, product_name for every active product (active = 1), sorted by sku.
hints: Only two columns are needed, both from products.
Active is stored as the integer 1, not as text.
SELECT ... FROM products WHERE active = ... ORDER BY ...;

title: Customer labels
prompt: Return customer_id and the customer's full name under the alias customer_label, sorted by customer_id. The column names are checked.
hints: An alias renames a column in the result, not in the table.
Use AS after the expression you want to rename.
SELECT customer_id, full_name AS ... FROM customers ORDER BY ...;

title: Distinct order statuses
prompt: Return each order status once, in a column named status, sorted alphabetically.
hints: Several orders share a status; you need each value only once.
DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.
SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders ORDER BY ...;

title: Cheap products
prompt: Return sku, unit_price_cents for products cheaper than 500 cents (any active state), cheapest first, ties by sku.
hints: Prices are integers in cents, so 500 means €5.00.
Cheaper than means strictly less than.
Sort by two keys: price first, then sku.

title: Orders needing attention
prompt: Return order_id, status for orders that are pending or cancelled, sorted by order_id.
hints: Two different status values qualify.
IN (...) is a compact way to write several OR conditions.
WHERE status IN ('...', '...')

title: Top of the org chart
prompt: Return employee_id, full_name for employees without a manager, sorted by employee_id.
hints: A missing manager is stored as NULL.
manager_id = NULL is never true. NULL needs its own operator.
WHERE manager_id IS NULL

title: Latest three orders
prompt: Return order_id, ordered_at for the three most recent orders. Newest first; break date ties by the higher order_id first.
hints: Sort first, then keep only the first rows.
Dates stored as YYYY-MM-DD text sort correctly as text.
ORDER BY ordered_at DESC, order_id DESC LIMIT 3

title: Premium shelf
prompt: Return sku, product_name, unit_price_cents for the three most expensive active products, price high to low, ties by sku.
hints: Filter to active products before ranking them.
LIMIT is applied after ORDER BY.
WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY unit_price_cents DESC, sku LIMIT 3

title: Product labels
prompt: Return one column named product_label in the form 'P01: Notebook' (sku, colon, space, product name) for every product, sorted by sku. The column name is checked.
hints: SQLite joins text with the || operator.
The separator ': ' is a text literal in single quotes.
SELECT sku || ': ' || product_name AS product_label ...

title: Catalog size
prompt: Return one row with two columns: customer_count (all customers) and product_count (all products).
hints: The two counts come from two different tables.
A subquery in the SELECT list can return a single value.
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ...) AS customer_count, (...) AS product_count;

title: Units sold
prompt: Return one row, total_quantity: the sum of quantity across all order lines (every status).
hints: Order lines live in order_items.
An aggregate without GROUP BY returns one row.
SELECT SUM(...) AS total_quantity FROM order_items;

title: Active price range
prompt: Return one row with min_price and max_price, the lowest and highest unit_price_cents among active products.
hints: Two aggregates can share one SELECT.
The filter runs before the aggregates.
SELECT MIN(...), MAX(...) FROM products WHERE active = 1;

title: Orders by status
prompt: Return status, order_count for each order status, sorted by status.
hints: One output row per status value.
GROUP BY creates the groups; COUNT(*) counts rows in each.
SELECT status, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY status ORDER BY status;

title: Repeat customers
prompt: Return customer_id, order_count for customers with more than one order (any status), sorted by customer_id.
hints: Count orders per customer first, then filter the groups.
WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.
GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

title: Revenue by payment method
prompt: Return method, paid_cents (sum of amount_cents) for each payment method that has payments, sorted by method.
hints: Payments already store the amount actually received.
Group by the method column.
SELECT method, SUM(amount_cents) ... GROUP BY method ...

title: Products with categories
prompt: Return sku, product_name, category_name for every product, sorted by sku.
hints: category_name lives in categories; products hold category_id.
Join on the shared key, and use table aliases to keep it short.
FROM products p JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id

title: Who placed each order
prompt: Return order_id, full_name, ordered_at for every order, sorted by order_id.
hints: Every order references exactly one customer.
An inner join is enough because the foreign key is NOT NULL.
FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

title: Employees and managers
prompt: Return employee (the employee's name) and manager (the manager's name, NULL when there is none) for every employee, sorted by employee_id.
hints: The manager is also a row in employees: join the table to itself.
An inner join would drop employees with no manager.
FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id

title: Never ordered
prompt: Return sku, product_name for products that never appear in any order line, sorted by sku. (The course dataset has none; the edge fixture has one.)
hints: Look for products with no matching order line.
After a LEFT JOIN, unmatched rows have NULL in every right-hand column.
LEFT JOIN order_items i ON ... WHERE i.product_id IS NULL

title: Paid order summary
prompt: For paid orders only, return order_id, line_count (number of order lines) and total_cents (sum of quantity × unit_price_cents), sorted by order_id.
hints: Combine a join, a filter and a grouping.
Multiply inside SUM, per line, using the price stored on the line.
JOIN order_items ... WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.order_id

title: Customer directory
prompt: Return full_name, email, city for every customer, sorted by full_name.
hints: Three columns from one table.
List the columns in exactly the order the prompt gives them.
SELECT full_name, email, city FROM customers ORDER BY ...;

title: Cities we ship to
prompt: Return each customer city once, in a column named city, sorted alphabetically.
hints: Two customers can live in the same city.
DISTINCT goes straight after SELECT.
SELECT DISTINCT ... FROM customers ORDER BY ...;

title: Category and active pairs
prompt: Return each distinct combination of category_id and active from products, sorted by category_id then active.
hints: DISTINCT compares whole rows, not single columns.
Select exactly the two columns whose combinations you want.
SELECT DISTINCT col1, col2 FROM products ORDER BY col1, col2;

title: Mid-priced active products
prompt: Return sku, unit_price_cents for active products priced from 1000 to 6000 cents inclusive, sorted by unit_price_cents then sku.
hints: Two conditions must both hold.
BETWEEN includes both ends of the range.
WHERE active = 1 AND unit_price_cents BETWEEN 1000 AND 6000

title: Paid orders of two customers
prompt: Return order_id, customer_id for paid orders placed by customer 1 or customer 2, sorted by order_id.
hints: Customer 2 has a pending order that must not appear.
AND binds tighter than OR.
WHERE status = 'paid' AND (customer_id = 1 OR customer_id = 2) — or use IN (1, 2).

title: Managed staff under 8 000 000
prompt: Return employee_id, full_name, salary_cents for employees who have a manager and earn less than 8000000 cents, sorted by employee_id.
hints: Having a manager means manager_id is filled in.
manager_id <> NULL never matches anything.
WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL AND salary_cents < 8000000

title: Two cheapest active products
prompt: Return sku, unit_price_cents for the two cheapest active products, cheapest first, ties broken by sku.
hints: The edge fixture adds a second product at the lowest price.
A tie-breaker makes 'the two cheapest' well defined.
ORDER BY unit_price_cents, sku LIMIT 2

title: Second page of products
prompt: Products are listed by sku, three per page. Return sku, product_name for page 2.
hints: Page 2 skips the rows of page 1.
OFFSET says how many rows to skip, LIMIT how many to keep.
ORDER BY sku LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3

title: Customers Z to A
prompt: Return full_name, city for every customer, sorted by full_name from Z to A.
hints: Descending order for text means Z first.
DESC goes after the sort column.
ORDER BY full_name DESC

title: Managers last
prompt: Return full_name, manager_id for every employee: employees with a manager first (by manager_id, then employee_id), and employees without a manager last (by employee_id).
hints: SQLite puts NULL first in ascending order, which is the opposite of what you want.
manager_id IS NULL is 0 or 1 and can itself be a sort key.
ORDER BY manager_id IS NULL, manager_id, employee_id

title: Line totals
prompt: Return order_id, product_id, line_cents (quantity × unit_price_cents) for every order line, sorted by order_id then product_id.
hints: Use the price stored on the order line, not the product's current price.
Arithmetic works directly in the SELECT list.
SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity * unit_price_cents AS line_cents ...

title: Ten percent off
prompt: Return sku, discounted_cents for every product, where discounted_cents is the price with 10% off, rounded down to whole cents using integer arithmetic. Sort by sku.
hints: 90% of the price, kept in whole cents.
Integer division rounds down; multiply before you divide.
unit_price_cents * 90 / 100

title: Prices in euros
prompt: Return sku and price_eur, the price as text with two decimals (1200 cents → '12.00'), for active products, sorted by sku.
hints: Divide by 100.0, not 100, to keep the cents.
printf formats a number as text with a fixed number of decimals.
printf('%.2f', unit_price_cents / 100.0)

title: Upper-case names
prompt: Return customer_id and name_upper (the full name in upper case) for every customer, sorted by customer_id.
hints: One text function does it.
UPPER changes ASCII letters.
SELECT customer_id, UPPER(full_name) AS name_upper ...

title: Longest names first
prompt: Return full_name, name_length (number of characters) for every customer, longest first, ties by full_name.
hints: LENGTH counts characters.
You can sort by an alias from the SELECT list.
ORDER BY name_length DESC, full_name

title: Who has a manager
prompt: Return one row with all_employees (number of employees) and with_manager (number of employees whose manager_id is set).
hints: Two different COUNTs over the same rows.
COUNT(column) skips NULLs; COUNT(*) does not.
SELECT COUNT(...) AS all_employees, COUNT(...) AS with_manager FROM employees;

title: Average salary
prompt: Return one row, avg_salary_cents: the average employee salary rounded to the nearest cent.
hints: AVG returns a real number.
ROUND without a second argument rounds to a whole number.
ROUND(AVG(...)) AS avg_salary_cents

title: Distinct buyers
prompt: Return one row, buyers: the number of different customers who have placed at least one order of any status.
hints: Customers with several orders must be counted once.
COUNT can count distinct values.
COUNT(DISTINCT ...) AS buyers

title: Categories with several products
prompt: Return category_id, product_count for categories that have more than one product (active or not), sorted by category_id.
hints: Count per category, then keep only some groups.
A condition on a COUNT belongs in HAVING.
GROUP BY category_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

title: Orders per month
prompt: Return month (ordered_at as YYYY-MM) and order_count (orders of any status) per month, sorted by month.
hints: The first seven characters of an ISO date are the month.
You can group by a computed value or its alias.
SELECT SUBSTR(ordered_at, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY month

title: Products that sell in volume
prompt: Return product_id, units (total quantity over all order lines, any status) for products with at least 3 units, sorted by units descending, then product_id.
hints: Aggregate order_items per product.
'At least 3' is a condition on the sum, so it goes in HAVING.
GROUP BY product_id HAVING SUM(quantity) >= 3 ORDER BY units DESC, product_id

title: Order city and status
prompt: Return order_id, city (the customer's city), status for every order, sorted by order_id.
hints: city lives on customers, status on orders.
Join on the customer key.
FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

title: Staff by team
prompt: Return team_name, full_name for every employee, sorted by team_name then full_name.
hints: Every employee belongs to one team.
employees.team_id references teams.team_id.
FROM employees e JOIN teams t ON t.team_id = e.team_id

title: What was ordered
prompt: Return order_id, sku, quantity for every order line, sorted by order_id then sku.
hints: order_items stores product_id; the sku is on products.
Start from the lines; each line has exactly one product.
FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id

title: Paid revenue by category name
prompt: Return category_name, revenue_cents (quantity × unit_price_cents of lines in paid orders) for categories with paid sales, sorted by revenue_cents descending, then category_name.
hints: Four tables: lines, orders (status), products, categories (name).
Join first, filter paid, then group by category.
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC, c.category_name

title: Order count including zero
prompt: Return customer_id, full_name, order_count (orders of any status, 0 for none) for every customer, sorted by customer_id.
hints: The edge fixture has a customer with no orders.
COUNT(*) would count the unmatched row as 1.
LEFT JOIN orders o ... COUNT(o.order_id)

title: Empty teams
prompt: Return team_name for teams that have no employees, sorted by team_name. (The course data has none; the edge fixture adds one.)
hints: Start from teams so every team is kept.
An unmatched team has NULL in every employee column.
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.team_id = t.team_id WHERE e.employee_id IS NULL

title: Paid orders including zero
prompt: Return customer_id, paid_orders (number of paid orders, 0 for none) for every customer, sorted by customer_id.
hints: A customer whose only order was cancelled must show 0, not disappear.
A WHERE on orders would turn the left join into an inner join.
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'paid'

title: Add a product
prompt: Insert product 20: sku 'P20', category 2, name 'Stapler', price 1800 cents, active. List the columns explicitly. The checker reads product 20 and then tries to insert another product with sku 'P20'.
probe: INSERT INTO products (product_id, sku, category_id, product_name, unit_price_cents) VALUES (21, 'P20', 2, 'Copy', 100)
verify: SELECT product_id, sku, category_id, product_name, unit_price_cents, active FROM products WHERE product_id = 20
hints: One INSERT statement.
List the six columns, then the six values in the same order.
INSERT INTO products (product_id, sku, category_id, product_name, unit_price_cents, active) VALUES (...);

title: Stationery price rise
prompt: Raise the price of every active Stationery product (category 2) by 10%, rounding down to whole cents with integer arithmetic. Other products must not change.
verify: SELECT product_id, unit_price_cents FROM products ORDER BY product_id
hints: Preview the rows with SELECT ... WHERE first.
Both conditions belong in one WHERE.
UPDATE products SET unit_price_cents = ... WHERE ... AND ...;

title: Cancel stale pending orders
prompt: Set status to 'cancelled' for pending orders placed before 2026-04-01. Leave every other order unchanged.
verify: SELECT order_id, status FROM orders ORDER BY order_id
hints: Two conditions: the status and the date.
ISO date text compares correctly with <.
UPDATE orders SET status = ... WHERE status = ... AND ordered_at < ...;

title: Remove an order completely
prompt: Delete order 106 together with its order lines, in an order the foreign keys accept. Nothing else may be deleted.
verify: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_id = 106
hints: The order lines reference the order.
Children first, then the parent.
Two DELETE statements: first FROM order_items, then FROM orders.

title: Archive cancelled orders
prompt: Create table archived_orders(order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ordered_at TEXT NOT NULL) and fill it with every cancelled order using INSERT … SELECT.
verify: SELECT order_id, customer_id, ordered_at FROM archived_orders ORDER BY order_id
hints: Two statements: CREATE TABLE, then INSERT.
INSERT can take its rows from a SELECT instead of VALUES.
INSERT INTO archived_orders (order_id, customer_id, ordered_at) SELECT ... FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled';

title: Top three paid orders
prompt: Return order_id, full_name, total_cents (sum of quantity × unit_price_cents) for the three paid orders with the highest total, highest first, ties by order_id.
hints: Total per order first, then sort and limit.
Join customers for the name; group by the order.
GROUP BY o.order_id, c.full_name ORDER BY total_cents DESC, o.order_id LIMIT 3

title: Paying customers
prompt: Return one row, paying_customers: the number of different customers with at least one paid order.
hints: Filter, then count distinct customers.
A customer with two paid orders counts once.
COUNT(DISTINCT ...) with a WHERE on status.

title: Revenue by payment month
prompt: Return month (paid_at as YYYY-MM) and received_cents (sum of payments.amount_cents) per month, sorted by month.
hints: This report uses payments, not order lines.
Group by the month part of paid_at.
SELECT SUBSTR(paid_at, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(amount_cents) ... GROUP BY month

title: Best sellers by units
prompt: Return sku, units (total quantity on lines of paid orders) for the three best-selling products, most units first, ties by sku.
hints: Units from pending orders don't count.
Join lines, orders and products; group by product.
WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.sku ORDER BY units DESC, p.sku LIMIT 3

title: Revenue by city
prompt: Return city, revenue_cents (paid order lines of customers in that city) for cities with paid revenue, sorted by revenue_cents descending, then city.
hints: The grain is one row per city.
Chain customers → orders → order_items.
WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY revenue_cents DESC, c.city
